summary: Thomas Burrow was an Indology and linguistics scholar. Educated at Queen Elizabeth School, Christ's College, Cambridge, SOAS, and Annamalai under P. S. Subrahmanya Sastri and Edward James Rapson, he held posts at the British Museum, SOAS, and Oxford.

Thomas Christian Tychsen was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at Kiel University (~1777–1779) and the University of Göttingen (~1779–1783), where he later served on the faculty from circa 1784 to 1834.
Thomas Cleary was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied under E. Bruce Brooks, completed a Ph.D. at Harvard University, and earned a JD at the University of California, Berkeley.

Thomas Doctor is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling Monastery and the University of Lausanne, supervised by Christian K. Wedemeyer and Tom Tillemans, and held a post at Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Thomas E. Crow is an art historian who studied at Pomona College and UCLA. He taught at CalArts, Chicago, Princeton, Michigan, Sussex, Yale, and USC, and served as director of the Getty Research Institute and professor at NYU.

Thomas Edward Colebrooke was an Indology and history scholar who was educated at Eton College and East India Company College. He served as President (1864–1882) and Vice-President (until 1890) of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

Thomas Ethelbert Page was a linguistics and history/archaeology scholar. He was educated at Shrewsbury School (~1864–1869) and St John's College (~1869–1873), and held a post at Charterhouse School from 1899 to 1936.

Thomas Freeman Yarnall is an Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies scholar educated at the University of Washington and Columbia University (Ph.D. by 2003 under Robert A. F. Thurman). He served as Executive Editor in Columbia's Department of Religion.

Thomas Henry Huxley studied at Great Ealing School, University College London, Charing Cross Hospital, and Imperial College School of Medicine. A scholar of philosophy, he held a post at Imperial College London from circa 1854 to 1885.

Thomas J. Mazanec is a Sinology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Calvin University, earned an MA at the University of Colorado Boulder, and completed a PhD at Princeton University under doctoral supervisors Anna M. Shields and Stephen F. Teiser.

Thomas Jarrett was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at St Catharine's College from circa 1823 to 1827 and served as Professor of Arabic at the University of Cambridge from circa 1831 to 1854.

Thomas Jülch is a Sinology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Goethe University Frankfurt, University of Hull, Heidelberg University, and University of Munich (PhD 2006–2011). He served as a postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University from 2013 to 2019.

Thomas Nathan Patton is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Cornell University, where he studied under Anne M. Blackburn, and held an attested post at the City University of Hong Kong in 2018.

Thomas Oberlies is an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Albrecht Wezler and Paul Thieme. He held posts at the University of Freiburg (attested 2001) and as Arbeitsstellenleiter at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Thomas R. Trautmann is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He held a post as professor of history and anthropology at the University of Michigan, attested in 1991.
Thomas Robert Malthus was an academic who studied at Warrington Academy (~1782–1783), Jesus College, Cambridge (1784), and the University of Cambridge (~1784–1788).

Thomas Roebuck was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who attended the Royal High School, Edinburgh. He was a member of The Asiatic Society (~1810–1819) and served as assistant-secretary and examiner at the College of Fort St George in 1811.

Thomas Watters was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He pursued his education at Queen's University Belfast, Queen's University of Ireland, and Queen's University at Kingston, graduating with a B.A. by 1861.
Thomas Zehnder is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He completed his PhD at the University of Zurich under the supervision of Alexander Lubotsky.

Thomé H. Fang was a philosophy and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Nanking and under John Dewey at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, later holding posts at National Central University (1925–1948) and National Taiwan University (~1948–1973).
